A portfolio for one person or one studio: the name, a captioned body of work, and the terms of working together.

`gallery` is the page's centre and the reason for the recipe: three to nine works, each with a title and a caption that carries information the title does not — what it is, for whom, when, at what scale. There are no image files; the caption is the work. `hero.object` is usually a wordmark or the person's own name; a sourced number or an exact quotation is used only when the material carries one.

Content requirements:

- The order is fixed and any subset keeps it. `prose` may repeat; a single quiet paragraph between the gallery and the terms is the usual shape.
- `quote` appears only with a verbatim quotation and a real attribution — a client or the person themselves. No invented testimonials.
- `cards` name the services or the terms of engagement; `cta` is optional and carries the one way to start a conversation. A portfolio does not have to sell.
- Captions are specific. Nine identical captions are a failed composition; three rich ones are better than nine thin ones.
- The page ends quiet before `footer`.
